text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Despite figures from the Australian Bureau of Statistics showing a growth rate of 0.9 per cent in yesterday's March quarter national accounts, the Federal Government continues to claim the economy will strengthen over the next year. The ABS figures reflect buoyant consumer spending, strong business investment, and an improving housing sector. Page 1.

A strong investment surge of A$280 million has left Queensland's oil shale twins Central Pacific Minerals and Southern Pacific Petroleum with a total capitalisation of more than A$2.4 billion, despite both never having produced a single barrel of oil from their ground in over 20 years of life as listed companies. Page 1.

National Mutual Holdings chief executive Geoff Tomlinson admitted yesterday the company's share price has suffered from investor uncertainty following the winning of a China life insurance licence by its French parent company Axa-UAP. While there has bee negative sentiments created towards National Mutual Asia, 69 per cent owned by the NatMut group, Tomlinson said the division is performing well. Page 21.

Following the announcement that it had sealed its A$3.4 billion share and asset deal with the Philippines' San Miguel Corporation, shares in Coca-Cola Amatil Ltd lifted 70 cents, or nearly 5 per cent to A$16.10 each yesterday. CC Amatil's shareholders wil be asked to vote on the deal in about a month. Page 21.

Federal Communications Minister Richard Alston is expected to announce the launch of an inquiry into the accuracy of billing data provided by Telstra to telecommunication service providers. The inquiry will be an embarrassment for Telstra in the lead-up to its sharemarket listing and will determine whether the telecommunications giant engaged in anti-competitive behaviour. Page 23.

The Australian Stock Exchange will introduce a health-care index within the next three months to measure the performance of the industry following strong growth in health stocks over the last few years. The index will comprise about 15 stocks including pivate hospital operators Australian Hospital Care Ltd, Alpha Health Care Ltd, and Healthscope Ltd. Page 25.
THE AUSTRALIAN

In a move that has launched a new onslaught against the big four banks, Australia's non-bank lenders yesterday cut interest rates on home mortgages and business loans. Financial services group Wizard Mortgage Corp led the charge, slashing its business and investment loan rate to 6.75 per cent. Page 23.

Analysts believe the boom in Australia's corporate bond market should continue over the next year, as falling money market interest rates force investors to look for higher returns from the private sector. Estimates place the corporate bond issues up a rcord A$5 billion since April. Page 23.

In a deal believed to be worth around A$250 million, News Corporation has apparently reached an agreement to sell its half share in Australian Newsprint Mills to New Zealand-based Fletcher Challenge. It is believed the two companies have reached a deal in principle, with only minor matters to be settled. Page 23.

In a move to get itself out of its involvement in Australis Media, Lenfest Communications has released a statement saying all its securities in Australia "are considered to be available for sale". The statement continues a trend of United States companie leaving the interactive Australian pay-TV arena. Page 23.

Rumours that the Commonwealth Bank is considering a share buyback scheme and payment of a special dividend drove shares higher yesterday. CBA shares were up 31 cents to A$14.27 at the close of trading yesterday after being as high as A$14.45. Traders, howver, are not convinced the rumours are true. Page 24.

Australian Stock Exchange managing director Richard Humphry said today that stock exchanges must confront the issue of competition without resorting to government protection. Humphry said that although market fragmentation, where buy and sell orders for the same security could be spread between different markets, has "undesirable consequences", stock exchanges had no alternative to trusting market solutions. Page 24.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Yesterday's national accounts show the manufacturing sector, the second biggest employer in Australia, is officially in recession after contracting for the second successive quarter in March. Federal Treasurer Peter Costello conceded the sector was rather flat, and blamed the high Australian dollar for the poor result. Page 31.

Yesterday's national accounts figures show economic growth in the agricultural, communications, construction and, to a lesser extent, transport sectors; but these are not important employment-generating sectors, which will hinder efforts to lower Australia's unemployment rate. Page 31.

Central Pacific Minerals and Southern Pacific Petroleum reported yesterday the first stage of an oil-from-shale project near the Queensland industrial city of Gladstone was about to start. This news sent shares in the two companies soaring, and left the mrket value of the companies at A$2.6 billion. Page 31. --

In what is the first move by any Australian bank into the A$4.5 billion private health insurance sector, the ANZ Bank and the National Australia Bank yesterday launched health insurance products aimed at being low-cost, add-on products. Page 31.

The Supreme Court heard yesterday that the Commonwealth Bank has "extended indulgences" to a former bank manager who appeared for the bank in a critical Supreme Court case won by the bank. Davridge Pty, which two years ago was ordered to pay A$9.3 million as a result of the manager's evidence, is seeking to overturn the judgment. Page 33.

Communications Minister Richard Alston has already drafted the terms of reference for an independent inquiry into the multi-million dollar dispute between Telstra and its service provider clients over billing. Alston is now looking for a consultant, accetable to both parties, to oversee the review. Page 33.
THE AGE

The latest national accounts released yesterday by the Australian Bureau of Statistics have indicated a deepening crisis in the country's manufacturing sector, with output dropping by 0.6 per cent in the March quarter, and 2.2 per cent in the first twelvemonths of the Howard Government. Page B1.

A junior-miner focused pooled development fund, Lion Selection Group, headed by Robin Widdup will provide a welcome A$150 million boost to the cash-starved junior mining and exploration sector. J.B. Were & Son will underwrite A$100 million of the issues, with Lion able to oversubscribe another A$50 million. Page B1.

Asahi of Japan, a new 14 per cent shareholder of Foster's Brewing, has sparked speculation of a shake-up of the Foster's share register after Asahi president Yuzo Seto said the group was considering a "completely new" relationship with the Australian grou. The news increases speculation that BHP's share of Foster's will be sold by the end of the week. Page B1.

After a two day visit to Mexico, Trade Minister Tim Fischer has made a commitment with Mexican Commerce Minister Herminio Blanco for the two countries to triple two-way trade by 2000 as a minimum. Fischer said the two countries wish to keep the wool pipeine open and possibly look into trade in other areas. Page B1.

Deutsche Morgan Grenfell has won the job as adviser to the Hogg committee in New South Wales, which has been set up to inquire into the social and economic merits of privatisation, and to inform community discussion. The move will place the company is a trong position ahead of the possible privatisation of the State's electricity industry. Page B2.

Victorian Treasurer Alan Stockdale said yesterday the State's three new gas retailers - Ikon Energy, Energy 21, and Kinetik Energy - are looking at retailing electricity and becoming "energy service businesses". Stockdale said that if the plans went ahead, consumers would receive one bill for both their gas and electricity use. Page B3.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
